page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n1 server family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 30.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place this server primarily in the weak to average tiers. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, rank in the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. Cryptographic and compression workloads show similar limitations, with single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the poor category. However, memory bandwidth for large blocks and Geekbench ray tracing tests achieve average performance levels.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-8 offers a balanced resource allocation profile suitable for legacy workloads or applications that do not require high-performance computing. Its dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent, albeit modest, execution speeds. The lack of local storage and GPU accelerators limits its utility for high-throughput database operations or machine learning training, though it remains capable of handling light web serving, basic software compilation, and small-scale text processing.
